Fix DONE_FOLLOWUP not firing: replace broken hash-based trigger with reported_done_tasks

causing hash comparison to silently match on subsequent runs. TASK-036/037/038
completions with screenshots were never reported to Slack.

Fix: Replace fragile done_seed hash comparison with direct check against
reported_done_tasks file (already maintained by aau_followup_done). If any
DONE task ID is not in reported_done_tasks, DONE_FOLLOWUP fires.

This ensures every completed task gets reported + screenshots uploaded,
regardless of hash state or file corruption.

Fix "says but never does" pattern: honest auto-reply, stale escalation, prompt fixes

Root cause: director promised action on Slack but coder agent silently failed
for hours. Three-layer fix:

1. Auto-reply changed from "確認します。ディレクターが後ほど対応します" to
   "受信しました" — no false promises before work starts
2. STALE_PROGRESS cooldown reduced 7200s→1800s, always notifies producer
   with task name + failure count (was silently swallowed by Ollama failure)
3. Director respond template: ban vague promises ("確認します", "対応します"),
   require specific action description in Slack replies

Combined with previous commit (consecutive failure tracking in agent_runner),
the system now escalates within ~15min of persistent failures instead of
silently retrying for hours.

Enforce quiet hours across all components, not just director_autonomous

Previously only director_autonomous.sh checked quiet hours. During quiet
hours (default 0:00-8:00), health_monitor alerts triggered inbox UNREAD
entries, which woke director_responder, which created tasks, which triggered
agent_runner — creating an unstoppable overnight loop.

Now all 4 components respect quiet hours:
- director_responder.sh: skip during quiet hours
- agent_runner.sh: skip during quiet hours
- health_monitor.py: log but suppress inbox writes and triggers
- slack_monitor.py: track message timestamps but skip inbox/replies
